sample_unit: AI-generated responses (43,325 simulated; 12,040 real-user; 111 adults in Study Two)

links.outcome: Prevalence of harmful, offensive or invalidating AI responses in simulated high-risk patient scenarios
links.effect: Clinician-verified AI content safety risk prevalence was 0.01% (95% CI 0.01%, 0.03%) across 43,325 responses; none encouraged self-harm, used offensive language, or invalidated users.
links.quote: In Study One (simulations), the prevalence of clinician-verified AI content safety risk was 0.01% (95% CI: 0.01%, 0.03%); no responses encouraged self-harm, used offensive language, or actively invalidated users.

links.outcome: Safety risk in real-user responses under multi-agent safety system with automated harm detection and clinician oversight
links.effect: No AI-generated responses among 12,040 real-user responses contained AI content safety risk (95% CI 0.00%, 0.04%); no serious adverse events occurred.
links.quote: In Study Two (observational study), no AI-generated responses were identified as containing AI content safety risk (95% CI: 0.00%, 0.04%), and no serious adverse events occurred.

unlisted_practices: Rapid-cycle in silico simulation with synthetic high-risk patients paired with continuous real-world monitoring
Constrained generative AI architecture delivering structured CBT skills training

screen.reason: The study directly evaluates the safety performance of a multi-agent safety system (automated harm detection, synthetic high-risk simulation testing, and clinician oversight) implemented on a patient-facing generative AI care agent in both simulated and real prospective human deployment.

primary.practice: multi-agent safety guardrails and continuous real-world monitoring
